Let q_1<q_2<… be primes with q_{n+1}−q_n ≥ q_n−q_{n−1}. Then liminf q_n/n² ≥ 1/κ'_S for
S={3,5,7,11,13}, where κ'_S = (ρ_S+E0_S)/M, M=15015, ρ_S=18748, E0_S=15.13085 (defined below); numerically
liminf q_n/n² ≥ 0.80024. Also (same method) S={3,5,7}: ρ=156, ≥0.63555; S={3,…,11}: ρ=1596, ≥0.71859.

Let P ≥ 1 and r* ∈ Z/P, and let m(r*) = 2 and m(r) = 1 for r ≠ r* (one repeated gap per period, average
multiplicity 1 + 1/P). This pattern is never Ẑ-good: it fails mod some prime ≤ max(7, P).

Let w(k) = loglog k/log k. Fix ε ∈ (0,1). There is N₀(ε) such that for all N ≥ N₀, the number of n ≤ N for which there is NO k ∈ (K/2, K] with ω(n+k)·w(k) ≥ (ε/10)·logloglog N is at most N·exp(−(log N)^{1−ε}). Here K = ⌊(log N)^{1−ε/2}⌋. In particular F(n) ≥ (ε/10)·logloglog N for all n ≤ N outside a set of that size. For each fixed C the same bound holds for #{n ≤ N : F(n) < C} once N ≥ N₀(C, ε).

Let w(k)=log log k/log k. There is an effectively computable N0 such that for every n ≥ N0 there is k with
17 ≤ k ≤ 30046 and ω(n+k)·w(k) ≥ 7·w(30046) > 1.58403. Hence F(n) ≥ 1.584 for n ≥ N0, i.e. liminf F(n) ≥ 1.584.

Write L3 = logloglog N, and let E_C(N) = {n ≤ N : F(n) < C}, with F(n) = sup_k ω(n+k)·w(k) and w(k) = loglog k/log k.
(a) For every fixed C > 0, |E_C(N)| ≤ N·exp(−(log N)^{1−(C+o(1))/L3}) as N → ∞.
(b) For every fixed θ ∈ (0,1) and θ' > θ, |E_{θ·L3}(N)| ≤ N·exp(−(log N)^{1−θ'}) for N ≥ N₀(θ, θ').
There is N₀ (effective in principle) such that for every n ≥ N₀ there is some k with 4 ≤ k ≤ 30033 and ω(n+k)w(k) ≥ 7w(30033) = 1.58406915…. Hence liminf F(n) ≥ 7w(30033).
